title: Module 7: Basis of design, actions and Eurocode philosophy
shortTitle: Basis of design, actions and Eurocode philosophy
whyItMatters: Connects first-principles structural mechanics to the semi-probabilistic Eurocode reliability framework (BS EN 1990 and BS EN 1991 + UK National Annexes) and establishes the 9-step engineering calculation workflow.
introduction: Covers the Eurocode philosophy of limit states (ULS and SLS), characteristic values (F_k, X_k), partial safety factors (γ_F, γ_M), design values (F_d, X_d), design action effects vs design resistance (E_d ≤ R_d), classification of actions (permanent, variable imposed, snow, wind, construction, accidental, thermal, earth/water), combination factors (ψ_0, ψ_1, ψ_2), the role of National Annexes, and the 9-step calculation workflow (Example 7.1).
objectives: Distinguish characteristic values from design values and explain why partial factors γ_F and γ_M exist.
Classify permanent, variable, and accidental actions and explain why ULS and SLS combinations differ.
Apply the 9-step Eurocode calculation workflow to take a floor beam from characteristic surface loads to ULS and SLS design action effects (Example 7.1).
learningGate: Explain why characteristic actions are not automatically the same as design actions.,Explain why ULS and SLS use different load combinations.,Explain clearly what "design action effect" (E_d) and "design resistance" (R_d) mean.,Set out a complete, structured 9-step design basis for a simple structural element.

topics.title: Eurocode Design Philosophy, Characteristic vs Design Values & National Annexes

Role of National Annexes (Nationally Determined Parameters, NDPs)

questions.prompt: In Eurocode design (BS EN 1990), why is a characteristic action F_k multiplied by a partial factor γ_F to obtain the design action F_d = γ_F · F_k for Ultimate Limit State checks?
options: From the Tresca maximum shear stress yield criterion combined with an empirical shear-lag reduction factor across the rolled web root fillets, assuming that because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel

To account for the possibility of unfavourable deviations of actions from their representative characteristic values, inaccurate load modelling assumptions, and uncertainties in assessing the action effects

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory
To calculate the instantaneous serviceability deflection

questions.prompt: In the fundamental Ultimate Limit State verification E_d ≤ R_d, what do E_d and R_d specifically represent?

E_d is the unfactored floor pressure in kN/m² and R_d is the span length

E_d is the internal force, moment, or stress (e.g. M_Ed, V_Ed, N_Ed) produced in the member by the factored design actions, while R_d is the maximum capacity (e.g. M_Rd, V_Rd, N_b,Rd) of the member calculated using design material strengths X_k / γ_M
E_d and R_d both represent serviceability deflection in mm

questions.learningObjective: Recognise dangerous error of applying γ_G,unfav = 1.35 to a favourable stabilising dead load
questions.prompt: When checking whether a light roof or temporary hoarding block will uplift or overturn under wind load, the self-weight G_k of the roof/block resists the wind uplift. What error occurs if an engineer multiplies the stabilising self-weight G_k by 1.35?
questions.assumptions: Critical Eurocode safety concept for both permanent and temporary works.
options: Because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel

Multiplying a stabilising (favourable) permanent action by 1.35 artificially inflates the restoring weight by 35%, which is non-conservative and dangerous; favourable permanent actions must use the reduced factor γ_G,fav (e.g. 1.0 or 0.9 in EQU) in accordance with BS EN 1990

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory
Wind uplift only occurs at the Serviceability Limit State
questions.explanation: When permanent weight helps prevent failure (favourable action), overestimating its weight is unsafe; BS EN 1990 assigns a lower partial factor (γ_G,fav) to favourable permanent actions.

questions.learningObjective: Explain physical rationale for combination factor ψ_0 on accompanying variable actions
questions.prompt: When a building is subjected to two independent variable actions (for example, imposed office floor live load Q_1 and extreme 50-year wind load Q_2), why is the accompanying variable action multiplied by a reduction factor ψ_0 (typically 0.5 to 0.7) rather than applying full unreduced peak values of both simultaneously?
questions.assumptions: Explains accompanying actions in BS EN 1990.
options: Because wind stops blowing whenever people enter an office building, assuming that it redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface

It increases the elastic Euler critical buckling load by halving the effective buckling length between inflection points, provided that the connection detail transfers full axial thrust without slip or local web crippling

Because the statistical probability that two independent time-varying actions both reach their rare 50-year extreme peak values at the exact same instant is much lower than either one peaking while the other is at its combination value ψ_0·Q_k
Because Eurocode ignores wind on multi-storey buildings
questions.explanation: Turkstra’s rule in structural reliability: one variable action is taken as the leading variable action at full γ_Q·Q_k,1 while accompanying independent variable actions are taken at γ_Q·ψ_0,i·Q_k,i.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate total characteristic permanent line load including beam self-weight (Example 7.1)

questions.learningObjective: Match ULS and SLS line loads to their respective design checks (Example 7.1)
questions.prompt: For a simply supported floor beam, load takedown gives a factored ULS line load w_Ed = 7.74 kN/m, an unfactored characteristic total SLS line load (g_k + q_k = 5.4 kN/m), and an unfactored characteristic variable SLS line load (q_k = 3.0 kN/m). questions.assumptions: Completes the bridge from Module 7 to Module 8.
options: The unfactored 3.0 kN/m line load is used for ULS collapse checks and the 7.74 kN/m load is used for SLS deflection, assuming that because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel

The ULS line load (7.74 kN/m) is used for bending resistance, shear resistance, web bearing, and support connection strength checks; the unfactored SLS line loads (3.0 kN/m variable and 5.4 kN/m total) are used for serviceability deflection checks
Only the 2.4 kN/m permanent load is used for all checks
All checks use 7.74 kN/m multiplied by another factor of 1.5
questions.explanation: Directly answers the final prompt of Syllabus Example 7.1 ("state which checks the line loads will be used for"). Engineering synthesis for "Match ULS and SLS line loads to their respective design checks (Example 7.1)": always trace the complete load path from point of application to the foundations, ensure compatibility between analysis boundary assumptions and physical site detailing, and verify against BS EN 1990:2002+A1 (Eurocode 0: Basis of Structural Design, Cl. 6.4.3.2 & UK NA).

hints: First Hint (Governing Structural Principle: Identify why standard editions and National Annexes must never be guessed): Follow the structured 9-part calculation workflow: convert characteristic area actions (kN/m²) via tributary width into line actions (kN/m), add self-weight, apply ULS/SLS factors, and compute design internal actions.

Second Hint (Analytical Elimination Criterion): Compute g_k,total = g_k,floor · b_trib + g_sw and q_k = q_k,floor · b_trib; then evaluate w_Ed = 1.35·g_k,total + 1.50·q_k, V_Ed = w_Ed·L/2, M_Ed = w_Ed·L²/8, and SLS δ = 5·q_k·L⁴/(384·E·I). Eliminate distractors that violate equilibrium, confuse elastic stiffness (E·I) with yield strength (f_y), or misapply Eurocode limit-state rules (Ref: IStructE Manual Ch. 2–3 & BS EN 1991-1-1 Cl. 6.3.1).

moduleAssessmentQuestions.learningObjective: Synthesise the purpose of Module 7 before starting Module 8
moduleAssessmentQuestions.prompt: What is the complete set of load takedown and structural analysis outputs from a BS EN 1990 basis-of-design calculation that must be handed over to perform a BS EN 1993-1-1 steel beam verification?
options: The member is verified solely for Ultimate Limit State cross-sectional yield resistance at midspan while relying on friction alone at the bearings to resist horizontal thermal expansion, wind drag, and notional lateral equivalent forces when evaluated under unfactored serviceability actions across the gross cross-section without partial safety factors or second-order geometric slenderness reductions

The structural analysis models the joint as a frictionless pin for vertical gravity load takedown but simultaneously assumes full rotational fixity when evaluating lateral storey drift and global second-order sway stability

The design substitutes the characteristic 95th-percentile material strength in place of the 5th-percentile characteristic strength and omits the combination factor ψ_0 when superimpose-combining independent variable wind and imposed floor actions

A clearly defined structural idealisation (span, supports, restraint assumption, load path), classified characteristic permanent and variable actions (including self-weight), and verified ULS design action effects (M_Ed, V_Ed, support reactions) alongside unfactored SLS deflection actions
moduleAssessmentQuestions.explanation: Module 7 establishes the entire "action and action-effect" side (E_d and SLS loads) so Module 8 can focus on EC3 member resistance (R_d), serviceability, and detailing.
